screenSummary.playArea: Graph of f near a, with a probe on each side of a.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a function, zoom, read the table of values, and predict the limit.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the probes toward a from both sides. Predict the limit, then check.

screenSummary.playArea: Graph with an open input band around a and an output band around the target L.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a function and set L, ε and δ with the sliders or by dragging on the graph.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a target L. Can you keep every nearby output within ε of L?

lesson.trySmaller: Set L to the limit, then shrink δ until no output leaves the ε-band.
lesson.challenge: Is there any L that works? Shrink δ and watch for a counterexample.
lesson.pass: The inequality holds at every input in the open band.
lesson.inputBand: Vertical dashed lines mark x = a − δ and x = a + δ; x = a itself is left out.
lesson.outputBand: Horizontal dashed lines mark L − ε and L + ε.
lesson.customNote: Drag the branches and the point. The limit exists when the branches meet, whatever f(0) is.
lesson.challengePrompt: With ε = {{epsilon}}, find the largest δ that works.
lesson.correct: Correct: that is the largest δ, to 0.001.
lesson.tooWide: Too wide: an input in the band leaves the ε-band.
lesson.tooSmall: That δ works, but a larger one would too.
lesson.plusInfinityAnswer: f(x) grows without bound, so the limit is +∞.
lesson.minusInfinityAnswer: f(x) falls without bound, so the limit is −∞.
lesson.sidesDifferAnswer: the one-sided limits are {{left}} and {{right}}, so the limit does not exist.
lesson.oscillatesAnswer: f(x) keeps swinging between −1 and 1, so the limit does not exist.
